Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

  "narrative": "This first proposal set focuses on direct, biologically motivated dependencies in a lung cancer cell line panel, while also testing a co-mutation interaction and one constructed marker. The strongest a priori claims are pathway-specific: KRAS-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on KRAS; BRAF V600E-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on BRAF; amplified receptor tyrosine kinases should show enhanced dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; MSI-high cells should show WRN dependency; SWI/SNF-deficient cells with SMARCA4 loss should show enhanced dependency on the SMARCA2 paralog; TP53-loss cells should show weaker MDM2 dependency because MDM2 inhibition is less effective when p53 is already inactive; and KEAP1-loss cells may be more dependent on NFE2L2 activity. For KRAS-mutant cells, I also expect weaker dependency on the related GTPase RIT1 because the direct KRAS oncogenic driver may reduce reliance on redundant RAS-family nodes. MYC amplification is used to probe replication/mitotic stress dependencies, with enhanced KIF18A dependency as an example. record.narrative: This first proposal set focuses on direct, biologically motivated dependencies in a lung cancer cell line panel, while also testing a co-mutation interaction and one constructed marker. The strongest a priori claims are pathway-specific: KRAS-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on KRAS; BRAF V600E-mutant cells should be more strongly dependent on BRAF; amplified receptor tyrosine kinases should show enhanced dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; MSI-high cells should show WRN dependency; SWI/SNF-deficient cells with SMARCA4 loss should show enhanced dependency on the SMARCA2 paralog; TP53-loss cells should show weaker MDM2 dependency because MDM2 inhibition is less effective when p53 is already inactive; and KEAP1-loss cells may be more dependent on NFE2L2 activity. For KRAS-mutant cells, I also expect weaker dependency on the related GTPase RIT1 because the direct KRAS oncogenic driver may reduce reliance on redundant RAS-family nodes. MYC amplification is used to probe replication/mitotic stress dependencies, with enhanced KIF18A dependency as an example. Finally, research marker F is tested as a constructed but potentially informative subgroup; if associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, it could define a candidate subgroup for follow-up, though it has no assigned biological role. All claims are initially unresolved and will be judged by effect size relative to clinical importance, uncertainty, and subgroup counts.

record.narrative: The first discovery panel produced three unusually large effects and several small/null effects. Because all estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, positive values support the original claim and negative values oppose it. H6 (MSI-high versus non-MSI on dependency_WRN, direction -1) has signed estimate +0.790 with 95% Welch interval +0.760 to +0.819 and cell counts 130 vs 1870. The raw contrast is therefore strongly negative: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency. This is several outcome SDs and far above a 10% relative scale, so I accept it. H8 (SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-WT on dependency_SMARCA2, direction -1) has signed estimate +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803 and balanced exposure n=412 vs 1588. This supports the synthetic-lethal paralog hypothesis and is robust in magnitude and sample size, so I accept it and request independent validation as the single most important confirmatory target. H9 (KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-WT on dependency_NFE2L2, direction -1) has signed estimate -0.796 with interval -0.816 to -0.776; the raw contrast is positive, indicating weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells, opposite to the registered prediction. I therefore reject the original H9 and register a reversed refinement for future testing/validation. The remaining effects are small relative to the dependency-score scale and do not justify acceptance. H3 is rejected because BRAF V600E did not show stronger BRAF dependency; the signed interval is compatible with a small opposite direction. H1 and H4 are biologically important but only borderline: H1 KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency and H4 EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency show point estimates in the predicted direction but intervals include null and near-null values, so they remain active unresolved. references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H8 is highly concordant with the discovery result. H8 is SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4 wild type on dependency_SMARCA2 with direction -1, so the reported signed estimate is +0.784 in discovery and +0.7925 in validation, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is strongly negative and the exposed SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The validation interval is +0.7627 to +0.8223 at the stricter independent-validation level, with cell counts 391 and 1609, so the effect is precise, large, and far above any reasonable 10% clinical-significance scale on this dependency score. I therefore keep H8 accepted and close the original investigation as adequately established in this dataset, while not claiming causality or outside generalizability. I also reassess the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 claim H20 using the parent evidence R9. H9 tested KEAP1 loss for stronger NFE2L2 dependency and was rejected because the raw contrast was positive. H20 has direction +1, and its displayed signed estimate is +0.796 with interval +0.776 to +0.816. This means KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-WT cells in this dataset. The magnitude is huge relative to the outcome distribution, so I accept H20 as a dataset-level finding, but keep it active for possible independent validation and specificity checks. Among the remaining first-panel results, H6 remains accepted and active pending validation; H1 and H4 remain unresolved active because their point estimates are in the predicted oncogene-addiction direction but are only borderline relative to uncertainty and the 10% clinical scale; H2, H5, H7, and H11 remain deferred unresolved because their intervals are too wide or their effects too small to accept. H3, H10, H12, and the originally directed H9 remain closed negative findings.

record.narrative: I corrected the previous registration error by linking refinements only to claims with available motivating evidence. The accepted dataset-level findings are H6, H8, and H20, so the most informative refinements test whether their effects persist after restricting to technical, p53, MSI, or histology contexts. For H6, I registered the MSI-high versus WRN dependency effect within Avana-library screens and within TP53-intact screens to assess whether the huge WRN effect is robust and not driven by library or p53-loss context. For H8, I registered the validated SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 effect within screen_batch and Avana-library subsets to test technical robustness. For H20, I registered the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 effect in TP53-intact and MSI-intact subsets to test whether the unexpected weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells persists in cleaner genomic contexts. The borderline KRAS and EGFR oncogene-addiction claims are refined to adenocarcinoma because these lesions are expected to be more dominant in that context. Finally, I added standalone specificity variants for NF1 loss on KRAS dependency within KRAS-mutation-free cells and BRCA2 loss on WRN dependency within MSI-intact cells; these are not marked as parent-linked refinements because the parent claims H13 and H14 currently have no evidence.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: I selected 12 claims that produce new discovery evidence and prioritize the highest-value follow-up after H6, H8, and H20. The set tests three things. First, it completes the next core panel of biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs: ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency, NF1 loss with KRAS dependency, BRCA2 loss with WRN dependency, TP53 loss with USP7 dependency, and MYC amplification with POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9 dependencies. These may reveal additional synthetic-lethal, pathway-redundancy, or transcriptional/translational dependency associations. Second, it tests robustness and specificity of the accepted MSI-high/WRN effect within Avana-library screens and TP53-intact screens. Third, it tests robustness and specificity of the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect within Avana-library screens and the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reversed effect within TP53-intact and MSI-intact screens. I deferred H23 because batch restriction is useful for technical robustness but library restriction is a stronger immediate specificity check for the SMARCA2 finding. I also deferred H27-H30 for now; if H13/H14/H17-H19 or the refinements are promising, those subtype or specificity variants can be prioritized next.

Iteration 3/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new panel separates into one large new association, several strong robustness checks for prior accepted findings, and several near-null or opposite-direction effects. Because returned estimates are signed to each hypothesis direction, a positive signed estimate supports the registered claim. H15 is the key new discovery: TP53 loss versus TP53-intact screens for dependency_USP7 with direction +1 has signed estimate +0.396, 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467, n=406 vs 1594. Since direction +1 corresponds to a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator difference, TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency (less negative scores) than TP53-intact cells. This is far above a 10% scale on the USP7 dependency distribution and is precise, so I accept H15 as a dataset-level association and request independent validation as the only voluntary validation this iteration. I did not validate H6 or H20 immediately despite their accepted status because their new subset analyses H21/H22/H25/H26 are highly concordant; H15 is a newly accepted claim with no independent confirmation yet and is therefore the higher-priority validation target. The MYC amplification panel is uninformative for the registered negative-direction hypotheses: H17 POLR2A signed estimate +0.004 with interval -0.017 to +0.025, H18 RPL11 signed estimate -0.012 with interval -0.034 to +0.009, and H19 DHX9 signed estimate -0.003 with interval -0.024 to +0.019 are all near null, and in each case the interval excludes a clinically meaningful effect in the predicted direction. I reject H17-H19 and close them. H13 NF1 loss/KRAS dependency signed estimate -0.020, interval -0.049 to +0.009, is small and opposite the predicted stronger KRAS dependency; because support is excluded beyond a clinically meaningful positive signed effect, I reject the overall H13 claim, though the already registered KRAS-mutation-free specificity variant H30 can remain for later review. H16 ARID1A loss/SMARCA2 dependency signed estimate -0.017, interval -0.057 to +0.023, does not support stronger SMARCA2 dependency; I reject the original H16 overall but register a refinement in SMARCA4-intact cells to test whether a weaker independent ARID1A effect can be detected once the dominant SMARCA4-loss effect is removed. H14 BRCA2 loss/WRN dependency is essentially null, signed estimate -0.0001, interval -0.045 to +0.045; the interval still includes positive support above the approximate 10% scale, so I defer rather than reject, pending the MSI-intact refinement H29. The robustness checks are strong: H21 MSI-high/WRN within Avana signed +0.794 interval +0.764 to +0.825; H22 within TP53-intact signed +0.780 interval +0.747 to +0.813; H24 SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 within Avana signed +0.781 interval +0.760 to +0.802; H25 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 within TP53-intact signed +0.792 interval +0.770 to +0.815; H26 within MSI-intact signed +0.798 interval +0.777 to +0.819. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
The H15 validation is highly concordant with discovery. H15 tests dependency_USP7 with TP53 loss versus TP53-intact screens under direction +1, so positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive: TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 scores and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery estimate was +0.396 (95% interval +0.325 to +0.467), n=406 vs 1594. Independent validation estimate was +0.395 with stricter interval +0.293 to +0.498 at alpha 0.003846, n=409 vs 1591. The validation interval excludes zero and a clinically trivial range, and the magnitude is approximately one SD of the dependency_USP7 distribution. Therefore I accept H15 and close its original investigation as a validated dataset-level association. I do not interpret this as proof that TP53 loss causally reduces USP7 dependency or that the association generalizes beyond this supplied dataset.

The current strongest supported findings in this dataset are: (1) MSI-high cells show markedly stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low/intact cells, H6 signed estimate +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819; this persists within Avana-library screens, H21 +0.794 (+0.764 to +0.825), and within TP53-intact screens, H22 +0.780 (+0.747 to +0.813). (2) SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H8 discovery +0.784 and independent validation +0.792 (+0.763 to +0.822), with Avana-library support H24 +0.781. (3) KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, reversed from the original synthetic-lethal-like expectation; the accepted reversed claim H20 has signed estimate +0.796 (+0.776 to +0.816), and the effect persists in TP53-intact H25 +0.792 (+0.770 to +0.815) and MSI-intact H26 +0.798 (+0.777 to +0.819). These are dataset-level associations measured from predictor status and CRISPR dependency scores, not causal statements.

Negative or clinically uninformative findings include H3 BRAF V600E not showing stronger BRAF dependency, H10 KRAS mutation not showing RIT1 dependency, H12 research marker F not showing STAT3 dependency, H16 overall ARID1A loss not showing stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and the MYC amplification panel for POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9 near or opposite to the predicted direction. H13 overall NF1 loss did not show the predicted stronger KRAS dependency. H14 BRCA2 loss was essentially null for WRN, but the MSI-intact refinement remains worth testing. Several unresolved items remain active because borderline effects or useful specificity checks have not yet been run: H1 KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency and H4 EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency are small but in the predicted direction, and their adenocarcinoma restrictions H27/H28 may determine whether the effects are context-specific or simply not clinically meaningful. H29 BRCA2 loss within MSI-intact screens and H30 NF1 loss within KRAS-mutation-free screens may refine the null overall effects. H31 will test whether the TP53-loss/USP7 association is robust within Avana-library screens. H32 will test whether ARID1A loss has an independent SMARCA2 dependency effect once SMARCA4-loss cells are removed; the newly proposed interaction will test whether ARID1A loss modifies SMARCA2 dependency within SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact complement. I also propose testing CDKN2A loss for dependency_USP7 as a p53-pathway extension: if CDKN2A loss also associates with weaker USP7 dependency, that would broaden the biological context beyond TP53 loss; if null, it strengthens the interpretation that the observed association is specific to TP53-loss status in this dataset.

The most informative next analysis batch is to run the accepted-finding specificity checks and the new pathway refinements: H31 for USP7 technical robustness, the new CDKN2A/USP7 comparison, H32 and the new SMARCA2 interaction for ARID1A/SMARCA4 context, H27/H28 for KRAS and EGFR histologic specificity, and H29/H30 for BRCA2 and NF1 specificity. H23 batch restriction is deferred for now because library restriction H24 and validation have already provided strong technical robustness for H8. In a later appraise, the highest-value validation request should likely be H20 because its reversed direction is scientifically important and remains unvalidated, followed by H6 if capacity remains.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

H13 overall NF1 loss did not show the predicted stronger KRAS dependency. H14 BRCA2 loss was essentially null for WRN, but the MSI-intact refinement remains worth testing. Several unresolved items remain active because borderline effects or useful specificity checks have not yet been run: H1 KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency and H4 EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency are small but in the predicted direction, and their adenocarcinoma restrictions H27/H28 may determine whether the effects are context-specific or simply not clinically meaningful. record.narrative:
No assessments are due at the analyze stage, so I am selecting 12 previously registered claims that give the highest-value new discovery evidence. The batch has three priorities.

First, I focus on the two active accepted central findings that still lack independent validation: H6, MSI-high associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, and H20, KEAP1 loss associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. For H6, H35 tests whether the MSI-high/WRN effect persists in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype, and H36 tests whether the MSI-high effect is modified by TP53 loss. Together these address histologic context and p53 co-alteration context. For H20, H37 tests technical robustness within Avana-library screens, H38 tests robustness in adenocarcinoma, and H39 tests whether the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is modified by TP53 loss. Because H20 has a large reversed effect, these specificity checks are important before accepting it as a broadly stable dataset-level association.

Second, I test the validated TP53/USP7 finding H15 for additional robustness and pathway specificity. H31 checks the TP53-loss effect within Avana-library screens, while H40 checks whether it persists among CDKN2A-intact cells. H33 tests CDKN2A loss itself as a predictor of weaker USP7 dependency. If CDKN2A loss shows a similar positive USP7 association, the p53-pathway context is broader; if CDKN2A loss is null but H40 remains positive, the validated association is more specific to TP53-loss status rather than CDKN2A-loss co-occurrence.

Third, I include focused new hypotheses and unresolved borderline claims. H41 tests STK11 loss as a predictor of weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and H42 tests STK11 loss among KEAP1-loss-free cells to determine whether any STK11 association is independent of the very large KEAP1-loss effect. This is biologically motivated by lung tumor-suppressor co-alteration patterns. H27 and H28 test KRAS-mutation/KRAS dependency and EGFR-amplification/EGFR dependency within adenocarcinoma, where oncogene-addiction effects might be more concentrated. These are useful because H1 and H4 were small but in the predicted direction overall and remain unresolved.

I defer H29/H30/H32/H34/H43 for this batch. H29 and H30 are refinements of near-null or rejected overall claims and are less urgent than central accepted findings and the new STK11 pathway hypothesis. H32/H34 test ARID1A/SMARCA2 context after the dominant SMARCA4-loss effect is established and after overall ARID1A was clinically uninformative. H43 tests TP53 loss on WRN among MSI-intact cells, but H36 already provides the most direct TP53 context check for the MSI-high/WRN effect. All analyses remain dataset association tests; causal or generalizable interpretation will be deferred.

All accepted claims remain dataset-level associations unless externally validated.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due at this explore stage, so I am registering refinements that improve on the strongest accepted dataset-level findings and add a few focused, falsifiable new predictor-outcome hypotheses.\n\nFirst, H6 remains an active accepted finding: MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency (raw contrast strongly negative; signed estimate under direction -1 is about +0.79). The new refinement tests whether this remains clinically meaningful in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. Expected raw direction is still negative for MSI-high versus non-MSI-high, because WRN dependency is already robust overall, within Avana screens, and within TP53-intact screens; if the adenocarcinoma subset estimate remains large and negative, this strengthens the specificity of the accepted association for the main population of these lung screens. I also register an interaction of the MSI-high WRN effect by TP53 loss. Because the TP53-intact subset H22 was essentially as large as the overall effect, the most parsimonious expectation is little to no interaction: the MSI-high effect should not be materially stronger or weaker in TP53-loss screens. An interaction near zero would indicate the MSI-high WRN association is not driven by TP53 co-loss status. A large signed interaction would suggest context dependence and would justify further subgroup analysis.\n\nSecond, H20 remains the key accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding: KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, accepted under direction +1. I add technical robustness within Avana-library screens and biological robustness within adenocarcinoma. The expected raw direction remains positive because the effect has already persisted in TP53-intact and MSI-intact subsets. I also add a TP53-loss interaction. Since KEAP1 and TP53 co-loss may occur in lung cancers, the TP53-loss interaction is an important specificity check: if KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 difference is similar with and without TP53 loss, the reversed association is more likely a direct or independent association rather than co-loss confounding. My initial expectation is roughly zero interaction because the TP53-intact subset effect was already nearly identical to the overall effect, but a positive interaction would still be scientifically interpretable as stronger weakening of NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss/TP53-loss contexts.\n\nThird, H15 is accepted and validated: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency under direction +1. I register a CDKN2A-intact refinement. record.narrative: The new results strongly support the already accepted central findings but leave most borderline or null extensions inconclusive. H31, H35, H37, H38, and H40 are large precise effects: TP53-loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency within Avana-library screens and within CDKN2A-intact screens; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma; KEAP1-loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in Avana screens and adenocarcinoma. These are not independent validation samples, but they are strong internal specificity checks and I accept them as closed robustness confirmations. H27 and H28 remain clinically ambiguous: KRAS mutation and EGFR amplification show small positive signed differences in adenocarcinoma, but the point estimates are near the 10% clinical scale and the intervals include both no effect and a borderline clinically meaningful effect. I defer them rather than accept them. H33 is near-null for CDKN2A loss and USP7 dependency; because the interval still includes a possible clinically meaningful positive association, I leave it unresolved but low priority. H36 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the MSI-high WRN effect. The subgroup exposed cell has only 24 observations, and the interaction estimate is small with an interval crossing zero and extending into meaningful positive values, so it is inconclusive. H39 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect; the estimate is near zero but not precise enough to claim no interaction, so I leave it unresolved and low priority. H41 and H42 provide no evidence that STK11 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency overall or in KEAP1-loss-free cells, but the intervals are not narrow enough to assert precise absence. I close these STK11 investigations as deprioritized inconclusive rather than as definitive nulls. I request independent validation for H20, the central reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association, because it is scientifically important and has not yet had independent validation. H6 has strong internal subset consistency and can wait until H20 validation is assessed.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

All accepted statements remain dataset-level associations, not causal claims or generalized biological claims.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due at this explore stage, so I am registering refinements that improve on the strongest accepted dataset-level findings and add a few focused, falsifiable new predictor-outcome hypotheses.\n\nFirst, H6 remains an active accepted finding: MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency (raw contrast strongly negative; signed estimate under direction -1 is about +0.79). The new refinement tests whether this remains clinically meaningful in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. Expected raw direction is still negative for MSI-high versus non-MSI-high, because WRN dependency is already robust overall, within Avana screens, and within TP53-intact screens; if the adenocarcinoma subset estimate remains large and negative, this strengthens the specificity of the accepted association for the main population of these lung screens. I also register an interaction of the MSI-high WRN effect by TP53 loss. Because the TP53-intact subset H22 was essentially as large as the overall effect, the most parsimonious expectation is little to no interaction: the MSI-high effect should not be materially stronger or weaker in TP53-loss screens. An interaction near zero would indicate the MSI-high WRN association is not driven by TP53 co-loss status. A large signed interaction would suggest context dependence and would justify further subgroup analysis.\n\nSecond, H20 remains the key accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding: KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, accepted under direction +1. I add technical robustness within Avana-library screens and biological robustness within adenocarcinoma. record.narrative: The newly released validations substantially strengthen the central evidence set. H8 (SMARCA4 loss and stronger SMARCA2 dependency) now has both discovery and independent validation evidence: discovery signed estimate +0.784 (95% interval +0.765 to +0.803) and validation signed estimate +0.792 with a stricter interval +0.763 to +0.822. The magnitude is very large relative to the dependency_SMARCA2 scale and far above the 10% clinical-significance scale. I therefore accept H8 and close it as a validated dataset-level association. H20 (KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency, the reversed-direction claim) is similarly strongly validated: discovery signed estimate +0.796 (+0.776 to +0.816) and validation signed estimate +0.806 (+0.775 to +0.838). This is a precise, large association and is consistent with earlier subset robustness checks. I accept H20 and close its primary investigation. Combined with previously validated H15, the strongest supported claims in the supplied dataset are now: SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These remain associations measured in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screens, not causal or externally generalizable claims. MSI-high versus MSI-intact remains an accepted active claim (H6) with very large internal effects, including Avana-library screens, TP53-intact screens, and adenocarcinoma, but it has not yet received the same independent validation treatment as H8, H15, and H20; it should be the next validation priority. Negative or clinically uninformative overall findings include BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation with RIT1 dependency, research marker F with STAT3 dependency, ARID1A loss overall with SMARCA2 dependency, MYC amplification with POLR2A/RPL11/DHX9 dependency, and NF1 loss with KRAS dependency. KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency and EGFR-amplification/EGFR-dependency remain small and borderline, including in adenocarcinoma, so they are not established as clinically meaningful. Interaction checks for TP53-loss modification of the MSI-high/WRN and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects are currently near-null but imprecise; the proposed new direct subset analyses test the exposed effects within TP53-loss screens, complementing the interactions. Next analyses should include these direct TP53-loss subset tests plus registered specificity checks such as BRCA2 loss within MSI-intact screens, NF1 loss among KRAS-mutation-free screens, ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact screens, the ARID1A/SMARCA4 interaction, and WRN association with TP53 loss among MSI-intact screens.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this explore stage, so I am registering new comparisons that are mostly context-specific refinements of the strongest accepted associations plus a few targeted oncogene/p53 pathway follow-ups. The highest-priority scientific issue now is whether the large accepted dependencies are robust to common lung co-alteration structure rather than being driven by correlated genomic or clinical contexts. For SMARCA2, the accepted H8 effect is huge and validated, but TP53 loss is a common co-alteration in lung cancers; the new TP53-loss-only SMARCA4-loss test will show whether the SMARCA4-loss association remains clinically large when TP53 co-loss is present. If it remains near the overall magnitude, it supports an independent SMARCA4-loss association; if it shrinks sharply, co-alteration context becomes important. For KEAP1/NFE2L2, the accepted reversed effect H20 should be tested among STK11-intact screens. STK11 loss is common in lung tumors and can co-occur with KEAP1 loss; preservation of the KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-intact cells would make a direct STK11-co-loss explanation less plausible. For USP7, the accepted TP53-loss effect should be checked among MSI-intact screens to ensure it is not a MSI-high co-alteration artifact. For WRN, the MSI-high effect is already robust in TP53-intact and adenocarcinoma screens; I add STK11-intact testing because STK11 co-loss is another plausible co-alteration context. A large positive signed effect under direction -1 would indicate that MSI-high status remains a strong WRN predictor when STK11 loss is absent. I also register targeted checks for borderline receptor-tyrosine-kinase and p53 pathway effects: EGFR-amplified versus EGFR-wildtype dependency among TP53-intact screens, KRAS-mutant versus KRAS-wildtype dependency among STK11-intact screens, ERBB2-amplified versus ERBB2-wildtype dependency among TP53-intact screens, and TP53-loss versus TP53-intact MDM2 dependency among CDKN2A-intact screens. These are useful because the overall oncogene and MDM2 effects were near the 10% clinical-significance scale or were imprecise, and co-alteration structure may mask context-specific effects. If the context-specific estimates remain small with intervals including no effect, I will treat these as non-clinically meaningful in this dataset. The next validation request should likely be for H6, the MSI-high WRN association, because it is accepted and biologically important but has not yet received independent validation. Existing registered active claims such as BRCA2 loss in MSI-intact screens, NF1 loss in KRAS-wildtype screens, ARID1A loss in SMARCA4-intact screens, the ARID1A/SMARCA4 interaction, TP53-loss WRN effect in MSI-intact screens, direct KEAP1/NFE2L2 effects within TP53-loss screens, and direct MSI-high WRN effects within TP53-loss screens remain valuable follow-ups. All proposals are dataset-level association tests, not causal or generalizable mechanistic claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
